findings.evidence: 'Then name the contrast and write the payoff (last line) first, then the setup.' Generic joke-writing advice the model already follows. It is activation content, not expert content.
findings.fix: Keep the audience and butt-of-the-joke questions, which are skill-specific. Shorten the payoff-first clause to a few words, or move it to references/text-memes.md (Pick a container section), which already restates it. Record the move.

findings.evidence: Step 1 branches only on an explicit text-only request ('greentext, copypasta, ASCII, "no image"'). No default is given for an ambiguous request such as 'make something funny for #eng-random' (one of the skill's own trigger queries).
findings.fix: Add one line to step 1: 'Unclear whether text or image: default to an image meme when the channel renders images (Slack, PR, docs) and to text when the user wants something to paste as plain text; ask only if neither applies.'

findings.evidence: "files": ["references/markdown-memes-guide.md"]. Several evals list the skill's own reference files as inputs. The 'files' field is meant for eval input files under evals/files/, so these entries test nothing extra and may confuse a runner.
findings.fix: Remove the reference paths from 'files', or move them to a separate field such as 'expected_reads' if a runner checks loading. Keep 'files' for real inputs under evals/files/ (for example a sample screenshot URL list for the background-415 case).

findings.evidence: `python3 scripts/meme_generator.py generate <id> '<caption>'... ` uses single-quoted shell arguments. A caption with an apostrophe ('don't deploy on friday', 'it's fine') breaks the quoting, so the command fails or splits captions. The skill's own escape table treats ' as a normal character.
findings.fix: After the usage line, add: 'Quote each caption in double quotes when it contains an apostrophe ("don't deploy"), or escape it as '\''; never pre-escape it to memegen form.' Add an apostrophe caption to tests/skills/meme-factory/test_meme_generator.py run_cli cases.
